title: Nonbossy mechanisms: Mechanism design robust to secondary goals
headline: Open finding: the single-item posted-price characterization fails at the extended zero-minus boundary.

work.title: Nonbossy mechanisms: Mechanism design robust to secondary goals

claims.label: Theorem 4 and its Theorem 5 proof step
claims.gist: The single-item PIC, numerical-IR and nonbossiness characterization fails at the extended 0-minus boundary.
claims.statement: Every primary-incentive-compatible, individually-rational and nonbossy single-item mechanism is a sequential posted-price mechanism.
conditions: Posted prices are nonnegative and universal rejection ends allocation.
claims.quantifiers: Every mechanism in the stated single-item class.

result.summary: A constant mechanism assigning bidder 1 the item at price zero is feasible, incentive-compatible, numerically individually rational and nonbossy, but not representable by a legal sequential posted-price mechanism at the all-0− profile.
result.witness: At the all-0− profile the constant mechanism allocates to bidder 1. A legal sequential posted-price mechanism cannot induce that allocation with nonnegative prices after universal rejection.
result.argument: The boundary outcome contradicts the sequential posted-price characterization while satisfying the listed mechanism properties.
not_claimed: The general PIC plus nonbossiness robustness theorem is not challenged.
The full proof under tie-aware individual rationality is not assessed.
result.repair_note: A tie-aware boundary condition may avoid this witness; the broader characterization is not established.
